solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unfinished dig on gray, dry sediment rich in nutrients

indicators.note: on puts the unfinished dig after the other two pieces

parts.note: Gy is the symbol for the gray, the SI unit of absorbed radiation dose
TT stands for teetotal, so dry in the sense of not drinking

indicators.note: unfinished means the word jab is left without its final letter

parts.note: a jab is a poke or dig

explanation.surface: An incomplete excavation on grey, dry ground full of nutrient-rich mud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gray' looks like a colour, but it is the radiation unit with symbol GY. 'Unfinished' cuts JAB to JA, and 'on' places it after GY and TT.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyttja is a Swedish-derived term for the organic mud that builds up at the bottom of nutrient-rich lakes.

clue.text: Pagan blasted hit single

indicators.note: something blasted is blown apart, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A heathen pop star's chart-topping record gets slammed or blasted out of speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blasted' reads as a curse on the record, but it is the signal to rearrange the two words that follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentilish is an archaic adjective meaning heathen, belonging to the gentiles rather than the faithful.

clue.text: Scotch bonnet provided core of invaluable antiviral protection

parts.note: a tam (tam-o'-shanter) is a Scottish woollen bonnet
'provided that' means if

indicators.note: the core of anything is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of a ten-letter word

explanation.surface: A fiery Scotch bonnet chilli is praised as a priceless shield against viruses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch bonnet' looks like the hot chilli pepper, but here it is literally a Scottish hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamiflu is the brand name of oseltamivir, a drug taken against influenza viruses.

clue.text: Mexican Tuber's current vlogging equipment used in short chat

indicators.note: used in means the current and the camera are set inside the shortened chat
short means the word jaw is cut by its last letter

parts.note: to jaw is to chat or talk at length
I is the physics symbol for electric current
a cam, short for webcam, is what a vlogger records with

explanation.surface: A Mexican YouTuber whose camera kit features in a brief conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuber' suggests a YouTuber, but it is a root vegetable. 'short' drops the last letter of the word for chat, and 'used in' sets the current and camera inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Jícama is a crisp, edible root grown in Mexico, sometimes called the Mexican turnip, so it is a Mexican tuber.

clue.text: Swindling beggar once having US cellist in knots following clash

indicators.note: coming after, so these letters are placed behind the next piece

parts.note: to jar is to clash or grate

indicators.note: what is in something is surrounded by it

parts.note: kn is the abbreviation for knots, a unit of speed
Yo-Yo Ma, the famous American cellist

explanation.surface: A con artist of old has an American cellist tied up in knots after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knots' suggests an anagram or tangle, but it is just the speed abbreviation, with MA tucked inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jarkman was a sixteenth-century vagabond who forged begging licences, so a fraudulent mendicant.

clue.text: Elder council judge what two Muslim states share about capital in Gulf

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge

indicators.note: to be about something is to go round it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: IRAN and IRAQ have IRA in common

indicators.note: a capital letter is the initial one, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A council of elders rules on what two Gulf-region Islamic nations have in common.
explanation.walkthrough: Iran and Iraq differ only in the last letter, so what they share is the first three letters. That IRA goes round G.
explanation.definitionFit: A jirga is a traditional assembly of tribal leaders in Afghanistan and Pakistan that settles disputes by consensus.

clue.text: Every time missing payment for using lots of money and coin, that of China

indicators.note: missing means the time letter is absent, and since every time goes, each of the three words loses one

parts.note: rent is the payment made for using property
T is the abbreviation for time; every one of the three words gives up its T
a mint is a large sum of money; with its time letter missing it gives these three letters
a bit is a small coin, as in a threepenny bit; with its time letter missing it gives these two letters

explanation.surface: A complaint that every payment for usage costs a fortune in cash, Chinese style.
explanation.walkthrough: T stands for time, and 'Every time missing' strips T from all three words: RENT, MINT and BIT become REN, MIN and BI. 'that' refers back to the money and coin of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Renminbi is the official currency of the People's Republic of China, so it is China's money.

clue.text: Old lady stuff one threads with knots

parts.note: one's old lady is one's mother, MA
to cram is to stuff
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An elderly woman stuffs and threads needles, tying knots in her craft.
explanation.walkthrough: MACRAMI is an older spelling of macramé.
explanation.definitionFit: Macramé is decorative work made by knotting cords or threads together in patterns.

clue.text: Number set up to block roaming

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to dam is to block a flow

explanation.surface: A figure is arranged to stop people wandering about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is the abbreviation, not a count; 'set up' flips the dam in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomad can be used adjectivally for wandering, living without a fixed home and moving from place to place.

clue.text: Gold-plated muck emporium cleared out with precision

indicators.note: plating coats the outside, so one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
dung is muck or manure

indicators.note: a room cleared out keeps only its shell, so just the outside letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A shop full of gilded rubbish is meticulously emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: The gold is the chemical symbol, split around DUNG. AD UNGUEM is Latin, literally 'to the fingernail'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase comes from sculptors testing a finish with a fingernail, so it means to a nicety, exactly.

clue.text: Customary feature of acoustic set?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, split in two words: an unplugged gig does without a microphone

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, NO MIC: an acoustic performance has no amplification. The question mark flags this playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomic describes ordinary conventional spelling or usage, established by custom rather than by phonetic principle.

clue.text: Stupid male quits amid mostly stupid bloomer

indicators.note: amid means the reduced first word sits in the middle of the shortened second
mostly means the word dumb loses its last letter

parts.note: dumb means stupid

indicators.note: quits means the male letter leaves the word moronic

parts.note: moronic means stupid

explanation.surface: A foolish man walks out on a rather dim flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' is a mistake in the surface but a flower here. Both 'stupid's do work: one is a five-syllable synonym that loses its male letter, the other a four-letter one that 'mostly' trims.
explanation.definitionFit: Doronicum is the genus of leopard's bane, yellow daisy-like plants, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Craving for news contained by following Arabian article

parts.note: what is contained by something is in it
f. is the abbreviation for following
an Omani comes from Oman on the Arabian peninsula
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A hunger for news is satisfied by an article from the Arabian press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contained by' looks like a container signal but simply supplies IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Infomania is an obsessive appetite for acquiring information, constantly checking messages and updates.

clue.text: Alpine antelope outstanding with leaves

indicators.note: what leaves departs, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: wizard is dated British slang for excellent
W is the abbreviation for with; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A remarkable mountain goat-antelope, pictured among the foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage but is a verb: W departs from the slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: The izard is the Pyrenean chamois, a goat-like antelope of the mountains of southern Europe.

clue.text: It's one hassle to pay a Norse goddess

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to dun is to pester a debtor for payment

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that it's a nuisance having to pay a Scandinavian deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hassle to pay' is a single idea: dunning is badgering someone for money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Idun, or Iðunn, keeps the apples of youth in Old Icelandic mythology, eaten by the gods to stay young.

clue.text: UK citizen behind story that probes Señora's very womanhood

indicators.note: a probe goes inside, so these letters are pushed into another piece

parts.note: muy is Spanish for very

indicators.note: coming behind means placed after, fixing the running order

parts.note: a story can be a fib or lie
a Brit is a British citizen

explanation.surface: A British journalist's intrusive story questions a Spanish lady's femininity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Señora's' signals Spanish, so 'very' becomes MUY, which then holds the Brit after the lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Muliebrity, from Latin mulier, a woman, is the condition of being a woman or feminine qualities generally.

clue.text: Difficult time exposed in cruel mockery

indicators.note: in places the stripped crisis inside the iron

parts.note: iron can mean harsh and unyielding, as in an iron rule

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer letters, losing the first and last

parts.note: a crisis is a time of difficulty

explanation.surface: Someone enduring a hard period laid bare to heartless ridicule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruel mockery' reads as one phrase, but 'cruel' is wordplay: iron in the sense of harsh, as in an iron fist, which holds the bared crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Irrision is an archaic word for derision, the act of laughing at someone, so it means mockery.

clue.text: Ash covering the world with lithium, sinking in parts over road to the north

indicators.note: heading north in a down clue means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

indicators.note: split into parts and laid over something, the word straddles another piece

parts.note: sagging, drooping
Rd is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Volcanic ash blankets the globe while a lithium-laden mass subsides over a northbound road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ash' is the tree, not volcanic dust. The reversal covers everything before it, not just the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Yggdrasil is the immense ash tree of Norse myth whose branches and roots link and overarch the nine worlds.

clue.text: Shadowy figure's read superficially when touring city in Uttar Pradesh

indicators.note: a tour goes all the way round, so one piece encircles another

parts.note: to skim is to read quickly and shallowly
Agra, home of the Taj Mahal, is in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh

explanation.surface: A mysterious character only half reads a guidebook while touring northern India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shadowy figure' suggests a sinister person; it is literally a picture made of shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A skiagram is an outline picture formed by shadows, also an old name for an X-ray photograph.

clue.text: Social recluse taking long walks on island of dragons at risk, never seeing last pair

indicators.note: never seeing last pair means the final two letters are dropped, and it applies to each of the three words in turn

parts.note: hiking is taking long walks in the country
Komodo is the Indonesian island home of the Komodo dragon; without its last pair it gives these four letters
risk without its last pair, the S and K

explanation.surface: A loner going on long hikes on a dragon-infested island, always at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never seeing last pair' trims all three words: HIKING, KOMODO and RISK become HIKI, KOMO and RI. The answer is a Japanese word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hikikomori is the Japanese term for people who withdraw from society and stay shut in their homes, social recluses.

clue.text: Filling of paprika, chorizo, lentils etc fried in pastry

indicators.note: a filling sits inside, so the answer lies within the run of words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and into the next

explanation.surface: A recipe: a spicy paprika and chorizo filling, with lentils, deep-fried in pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as part of the same recipe, which makes the whole clue look like a list of ingredients.
explanation.definitionFit: A kachori is an Indian snack of spiced lentil or other filling enclosed in a deep-fried pastry shell.

clue.text: With Khalkha evacuated there's no good place for the rest of the Chinese

definitions.text: place for the rest of the Chinese

indicators.note: an evacuated building is emptied, so only the outside letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters only
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Once the Mongolian Khalkha clear out, no decent spot remains for other Chinese.
explanation.walkthrough: Khalkha is the main Mongol people; 'the rest of the Chinese' sounds like the remaining population but means their sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A kang is a heated brick platform used as a bed in northern China, where people sleep and relax.

clue.text: An offer on one of the Breughels, City with a Lagoon

parts.note: a bid is an offer, as at auction
Jan Brueghel the Elder and Younger were painters of the family

explanation.surface: An auction bid is made on a Breughel painting showing a lagoon city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the bid above the painter, so it comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Abidjan, the largest city of Côte d'Ivoire, lies on the Ébrié Lagoon on the West African coast.

clue.text: Nice looking for some whiskey in Fenland city after six

indicators.note: coming after places these letters behind the preceding piece

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: what is in something is held inside it

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in the Fens of eastern England
Whiskey is the radio code word for W

explanation.surface: Someone in Ely after six o'clock fancies a nice-looking drop of whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling 'whiskey' is the giveaway for the NATO alphabet word for W.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewly is a dialect word for pleasing to the eye, attractive to view, sightly.

clue.text: Things done legally, not anything stopped by law

indicators.note: a hole stopped is plugged, so one piece fills the middle of another

parts.note: sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all
an act of Parliament is a law

explanation.surface: Legal acts in which nothing at all is prevented by the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet FA' (a polite form of a ruder phrase) means nothing whatsoever in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Facta is the Latin plural of factum, a legal term for deeds or acts performed.

clue.text: Fine American people — and some molluscs

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
US for United States, American
us, as in we people

explanation.surface: Praise for fine American folk, plus a few shellfish thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'people' is the pronoun us, not a nation, so the two USes come from different words.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusus is a genus of spindle-shaped sea snails, so the name covers a group of shellfish.

clue.text: Juristical brief perplexed top legal arbitrator

indicators.note: perplexed means confused, so the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order
brief means the word juristical is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A confused legal summary for a senior judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like a lawyer's brief, but it means shortened: JURISTICA, which 'perplexed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A justiciar was the chief political and judicial officer under the Norman and early Plantagenet kings of England.

clue.text: Ship's police officer has success apprehending foremost of navy's troublemakers

indicators.note: to apprehend is to seize and hold, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: in British usage, 'any joy?' asks whether you had any success

indicators.note: the foremost letter is the first, taken from each of two words

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A naval policeman succeeds in arresting the ringleaders of the navy's troublemakers.
explanation.walkthrough: JOY as success is British idiom: 'Any joy?' means 'Did it work?'
explanation.definitionFit: Jonty is Royal Navy slang for the master-at-arms, the senior rating responsible for discipline on board.

clue.text: Gliding like this across heavens, pull apart

indicators.note: stretched across something, the outer piece spans either side of it

parts.note: so means in this way
Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'Heavens!'
to rend is to tear apart

explanation.surface: Something sails smoothly through the sky, then breaks apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavens' looks like the sky, but it is an exclamation, the British 'Cor!'
explanation.definitionFit: Scorrendo is an Italian musical direction telling the player to slide smoothly from note to note.

clue.text: Without sauce, it's dire for Dubliners

parts.note: w/o is the abbreviation for without
jus is a thin meat gravy

explanation.surface: An Irish diner complains that a meal served without sauce is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Dubliners' marks the definition as local slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Wojus is Dublin slang for very poor or terrible, used of anything of bad quality.

clue.text: Declaration of selfhood, wearing coy loose undergarment

indicators.note: what is worn is wrapped around the wearer, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: coy and shy both mean bashful
"I'm me" asserts one's own identity

explanation.surface: A bashful person, in flimsy lingerie, asserts their own identity.
explanation.walkthrough: The declaration is the phrase I'M ME, which goes inside the bashful word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shimmey is an old variant of chemise, a woman's loose-fitting shift worn beneath other clothes.

clue.text: Service manual essential to plan my holiday's return

indicators.note: on the way back, the letters run from right to left
what is essential is at the heart, so the answer sits within the words

parts.note: letters running through the three words

explanation.surface: A guidebook is indispensable for planning the journey home from a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service manual' suggests a car handbook; the service is a church one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymnal is the book of hymns used by a congregation during a church service of worship.
